title: Service migration and graceful data settlement guidelines
author: Priya Menon
content:
Overview:
This page defines the recommended pattern, operational checklist, and observable contracts for performing service migrations and graceful data settlement at Redwood. It covers both stateless and stateful services, outlines live-drain semantics, defines SLA-safe cutover windows, and documents escalation and rollback procedures. The goal is to minimize user-visible errors and data loss while keeping throughput and cost within predictable bounds.

When to use this doc:
- Moving a service between clusters or regions.
- Replacing a service with a new implementation/version that changes state layout.
- Draining pods or instances for kernel/driver upgrades where in-flight state must be reconciled.
- Backfilling or resharding state (KV/redis, prefix caches, or local disk caches).

Key principles:
1) Interface parity first: ensure the new service supports the same external API and failure modes before migrating traffic.
2) Observe-then-change: add metric dashboards and tracing for the migration path prior to routing changes.
3) Idempotent settlement: design state settlement tasks to be idempotent and resumable.
4) Small increments: migrate in narrow slices (tenant, prefix, or % of traffic) with automated verification gates.
5) Fail open safely: define explicit fallback behavior if a settlement step fails (failover to old service, queueing, or backpressure).

Required pre-migration checklist (must be green before cutover):
- Ownership and schedule: migration owner, oncall, and rollback owner assigned.
- Rollout plan documented in PRD or migration ticket including slice size and cadence.
- Health dashboards created: request latency (p50/p95/p99), error rate (4xx/5xx), queue length, settlement throughput (writes/sec), and consumer lag for async pipelines.
- Automated smoke tests that validate core paths for both implementations.
- Migration feature-flag or routing policy in the service mesh that supports canary percentages and label-based routing.
- Data compatibility tests: byte-level compare for migrated keys (sampled) and logical validation (search results, counters).
- Backfill tooling packaged as idempotent job(s) with checkpointing.

SLOs and cutover safety thresholds:
- Error rate: must not exceed 0.5% additional user-visible 5xx errors vs baseline for canary slices.
- Latency: p95 increase must be <= 20% relative to baseline for canary slice.
- Redis/kv consumer lag threshold: <30s for stateful sync jobs during steady-state.
- Settlement throughput: must be >= 1.5x expected steady write burst for the tenant during migration window.
If any of these thresholds are violated for more than 5 minutes during a canary, abort and roll back.

Routing and traffic control patterns:
- Percentage canary: route X% of traffic (start at 1%) and verify metrics for 15-30 minutes.
- Tenant-based canary: select low-risk tenants and route all their traffic to the new service.
- Prefix sharding: for keyspace-partitioned services, migrate a prefix range and compare outputs for a representative sample.
- Shadow write + read-compare: write to both old and new service, but read from old; asynchronously compare new results to ensure compatibility.

Live drain semantics (stateful services):
1) Quiesce acceptors: stop accepting new mutable work for the draining shard/instance.
2) Flush in-memory state to durable store (S3, primary DB) with transactional checkpoints.
3) Replay or push outstanding operations to a settlement queue with explicit sequence ids.
4) Mark shard as read-only in routing layer until consumption of settlement queue completes.
5) Signal completion and release resources.

Example CLI runbook (stateful drain):
1) Set feature flag and routing: curl -X POST https://console.internal/flags -d '{"service":"payments","route":"tenant-42","percent":0}'
2) Trigger drain: 
   kubectl annotate pod payments-123 dry-run=true --context=prod-cluster
3) Start settlement job (idempotent): 
   ./bin/settlement-job --shard=shard-17 --checkpoint=/var/checkpoints/shard-17.chk --concurrency=8
4) Monitor metrics: 
   - grafana: /d/xxx/service-migration-dashboard
   - logs: journalctl -u settlement-job -f | grep shard-17
5) Confirm sample validation: run-sample-compare --from=old-service:api.old --to=new-service:api.new --limit=500
6) Final cutover (if checks pass): update routing percent to include the shard and reduce old traffic accordingly.

Data settlement job configuration examples (YAML):
| field | description | recommendation |
|-------|-------------|----------------|
| concurrency | number of parallel workers | 4-16 depending on DB CPU |
| batch_size | number of keys per checkpoint write | 100-1000 |
| checkpoint_interval | frequency of durable checkpointing | 30s |
| retry_backoff_ms | exponential backoff base | 200ms |

Example YAML snippet:
---
settlement_job:
  shard: "shard-17"
  concurrency: 8
  batch_size: 250
  checkpoint_interval: "30s"
  checkpoint_path: "/var/checkpoints/shard-17.chk"
  metrics_prefix: "migration.payments.shard17"
---

Validation patterns and sampling:
- Deterministic hash-based sampling: pick N keys using service-wide consistent hash to avoid bias.
- End-to-end functional tests: perform a canonical user flow (create -> update -> read) on the new service and validate against expected invariants.
- Time-windowed comparisons: compare outputs for requests received within the same 5s ingestion window to account for causal ordering.

Dashboard & alert essentials (create prior to migration):
- Migration dashboard panels: ingress rate, egress rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate (absolute and delta vs baseline), settlement queue length, consumer lag, checkpoint commit rate.
- Alerting rules:
  - migration:settlement_queue_growing (WARN) if queue grows >1000 for 10m -> notify SRE and owner.
  - migration:failure_rate_high (P1) if new-service 5xx delta >0.5% for 5m -> auto-rollover to rollback playbook.
  - migration:checkpoint_error (P0) any checkpoint write failure -> page oncall.

Rollback decision matrix (abbreviated):
- Immediate rollback (trigger if): P0 checkpoint failure, data corruption detected in sampling, sustained consumer lag >5m and rising.
- Timed rollback (trigger if): p95 latency increase >50% or 5xx delta >2% sustained >15m.
- Soft rollback (route reduction): reduce canary percent by 50% and re-evaluate for 10m.

Rollback procedure (rapid):
1) Set routing policy to route 100% back to old service.
2) Cancel ongoing settlement jobs and mark them for resume later (do not truncate checkpoints).
3) Restore write terminals to old service and unquiesce acceptors.
4) Create postmortem ticket and tag with migration labels.

Post-migration checks and retrospective triggers:
- Data reconciliation report: delta counts and checksum pass rate (>99.99% sampled).
- Cost delta: estimate per-minute CPU/GPU and egress cost variance and tag if >10% change.
- Error-mode analysis: record any new error types introduced by new implementation.
- User-impact window: annotate incidents with affected tenant list and duration.

Retrospective template (to run within 5 business days):
1) Summary: migration goal, scope, and final outcome.
2) Timeline: key events with timestamps.
3) What went well: automated checks, dashboards, test coverage.
4) What didn't: unexpected backpressure, missing metric, long rollback.
5) Action items: assign owners, due dates, and acceptance criteria.

Operational ownership and contacts:
- Migration owner: name and pager (example: Priya Menon, priya@redwood.ai, pager: +1-555-1001).
- Rollback owner: senior platform engineer (example: Liam Chen).
- SRE oncall: tagged in the migration ticket and alerted via LEX on any P0.

Security and compliance notes:
- For migrations involving customer PII or regulated datasets, coordinate with Security & Compliance for data masking and audit logs before migrating.
- Ensure KMS/HSM keys used by new deployment are provisioned and rotated following our key lifecycle policy.

Appendix: quick checklist (copyable)
- [ ] Owners assigned and oncall notified
- [ ] Dashboards created and shared
- [ ] Smoke tests pass against new binary
- [ ] Settlement job configured and dry-run completed
- [ ] Sampling/compare tool runs succeeded (>= 500 samples)
- [ ] Cutover window booked and stakeholders notified
